topic: When a GC-shard delta bucket is empty, the fold carries the parent generation's
canonical_claim: When a GC-shard delta bucket is empty, the fold carries the parent generation's `RunRef` without run I/O; zero run I/O requires both the delta bucket and retired state to be empty.; When a GC-shard delta bucket is empty, the new `fold_seal` carries the parent generation's `RunRef` key and checksum verbatim and performs no run GET or PUT for that shard. Additionally, `RunRef` has an explicit additive `shard` field so consumers associate a run with a GC shard without parsing key paths; run consumers resolve through seal references rather than constructing keys. Additionally, An empty-delta and empty-retired GC shard is pure ref-carry and performs zero run-object I/O; `RunRef` carries `shard` and `generation` and consumers resolve runs through seal refs.; A pure reference-carry path requires both an empty delta bucket and an empty retired-merge input; an empty delta with prior retired entries still runs the merge so retired entries settle every pass.; A shard may be pure-ref-carried only when it has no deltas and `condemned_total == 0`.

topic: source-edge in-degree
canonical_claim: The persisted in-degree authority is the set of active source edges identified by `(ManifestId, path)`, with edge IDs computed by `sourceEdgeId(ManifestId, path)`; `in_degree(blob)` is the cardinality of that active source-edge set during a round and is not persisted as a separate counter.; CAS blob in-degree is a SET of source edges with last-wins semantics per key, not a counter; an unmatched removal is a per-key no-op and cannot remove a sibling manifest edge for the same blob. Additionally, The in-degree reducer models source edges as a set: an unmatched `-1` is dropped as a no-op and a duplicate `+1` collapses, so the reducer must not materialize negative edges merely to repair the retention leak. Additionally, The unmatched removal-fold `-1` is harmless under the current edge-set model because source edges are set membership keyed by `(ref, ManifestId, path)`, not a counter; erasing an already-absent edge cannot affect another manifest's edges. Additionally, In-degree is a set-presence merge keyed by `(blob, source_id)` and applied in strict transaction-id order; a `del` whose key is absent is a silent no-op. Additionally, The source-edge reducer treats in-degree as a set: an unmatched `-1` must be dropped rather than materialized as a negative edge, because a negative edge could cause a false deletion.

topic: Only blobs with an explicit zero-transition marker in the current generation are
canonical_claim: Only blobs with an explicit zero-transition marker in the current generation are GC candidates; a blob never observed as a reference target is not a candidate.

topic: If a blob is already absent at condemnation time, GC records no candidate and ne
canonical_claim: If a blob is already absent at condemnation time, GC records no candidate and never fabricates a delete token from a 404.

topic: two-phase blob deletion
canonical_claim: Physical deletion is two-phase: a zero-in-degree or floor-eligible condemned entry is first published as `delete_pending` after surviving one full GC round, and the physical `deleteExact` runs only in a later pass for an entry pending in the previous published list; graduation requires confirmed `Condemned` evidence for the exact `(hash, token)`, recovery spares the entry, and a token mismatch leaves a newer blob untouched.; Two-phase graduation publishes `delete_pending` with a round CAS before physical delete, preventing a deposed leader's stale pass from deleting a live blob. Additionally, Two-phase graduation uses `delete_pending`: pre-CAS deletes apply only to previously published pending entries, and deletion lags condemnation by one pass.

topic: Generation pruning skips generations still referenced by the adopted seal, while
canonical_claim: Generation pruning skips generations still referenced by the adopted seal, while a later parent-reference hand-off deletes the entire superseded generation prefix after the CAS.; Retention must preserve any run object referenced by the live adopted seal; when a later pass replaces a parent reference, it deletes the superseded old-generation prefix after the CAS, with a crash window that can strand at most one small object per shard in the original design.

topic: Patch manifests are first-class reachability roots and keep both their own delta
canonical_claim: Patch manifests are first-class reachability roots and keep both their own delta blobs and referenced base-part blobs alive while active.; A patch-part manifest is a first-class reachability root that keeps both its delta blobs and the referenced base blobs alive transitively.

topic: `dropNamespace` appends a tombstone as its last journal event, and GC may reclai
canonical_claim: `dropNamespace` appends a tombstone as its last journal event, and GC may reclaim the shard object only after the tombstone and all prior journal events are folded; a token change from a revive prevents deletion.; The incarnation registry-removal model proves that a durable per-shard never-reused incarnation and a newborn shard self-floor at the current GC round are both required; neither coordinate alone suffices.; The shard-incarnation model requires reclaim to wait until the shard journal, including its tombstone, is fully folded.; The planned ref-shard reclaim condition is empty refs, a last journal tombstone, complete folding past the fence at the current incarnation, and token-guarded `deleteExact`.; A durable never-reused per-shard incarnation plus a newborn shard fenced to the current GC round replaces the namespace registry's safety role, but reclaim still waits for the shard journal to be fully folded.

topic: live GC-round graduation predicate is `condemn_round < current_round`, with `sup
canonical_claim: The live GC-round graduation predicate is `condemn_round < current_round`, with `suppress_destructive` independently blocking graduation on a clamped pass.; Graduation is determined by `condemn_round < current_round`, where `current_round` is `new_round = state.round + 1`; using `state.round` would prevent entries from graduating. Additionally, The rebuilt orphan rows use `CondemnedRow{token, size, condemn_round = minted_round}` and graduate when `condemn_round < current_round`, which is the next round after minting.

topic: `CaGcRoundDeferCore
canonical_claim: `CaGcRoundDeferCore.tla` permits a non-destructive round to defer rebuilding the in-degree snapshot, but a due graduation must force-fold before deleting and deferral must be bounded.; A due GC graduation must force a fold before physical deletion, while a non-destructive round may re-adopt the sealed in-degree snapshot; deferral is bounded.

topic: disaster-recovery rebuild starts with an empty retired list, over-protects until
canonical_claim: A disaster-recovery rebuild starts with an empty retired list, over-protects until the normal condemnation pipeline catches up, and mints its round above every surviving mount acknowledgement.; A successful rebuild publishes an empty `retired_refs` set, preserving the reconstructed snapshot and making all content pass through the normal condemn → acknowledgement floor → graduate → delete pipeline again.

topic: current regular GC round has request complexity O(delta) plus O(servers) and one
canonical_claim: The current regular GC round has request complexity O(delta) plus O(servers) and one `LIST` sweep, without an O(universe) GET or PUT phase.

topic: If a listed shard token matches the sealed folded token, GC skips the shard body
canonical_claim: If a listed shard token matches the sealed folded token, GC skips the shard body `GET`; clamped-coverage shards are never skipped.; `changedShardCount` is the number of present shards whose token differs from the sealed generation, represented by the non-`DiscoverDecision::Skip` decisions from `computeDiscoverDecisions`.

topic: newly condemned candidate receives one `HEAD` to capture its exact token, while
canonical_claim: A newly condemned candidate receives one `HEAD` to capture its exact token, while an already-condemned entry is re-verified from the fold and is not re-HEADed.; A blob candidate is HEAD-observed with an exact token when its edge set becomes empty; a carried candidate pays no HEAD, and missing bodies are non-throwing while present-but-invalid bodies are `CORRUPTED_DATA`.; A zero-in-degree candidate not already retired is condemned by HEADing its blob, capturing its current token, and appending `(hash, token, K)` to the retired output; an absent blob is skipped.

topic: Snapshot-run consumers use one `HEAD`, one ranged tail `GET`, and one streaming
canonical_claim: Snapshot-run consumers use one `HEAD`, one ranged tail `GET`, and one streaming body `GET`; a large footer may add one exact-footer ranged `GET`.; The intended streaming open profile is exactly one HEAD, one tail ranged GET, and one body `getStream`; `seek` adds one ranged GET per touched block.

topic: Snapshot-run streaming uses O(block) resident memory with a maximum current bloc
canonical_claim: Snapshot-run streaming uses O(block) resident memory with a maximum current block size of 1 MiB, independent of run size.; `RunFileReader` has borrowed-memory and streaming modes; streaming mode retains only the footer index and one current block no larger than `kRunHardCapBlockSize` = 1 MiB, while `seek` uses a ranged GET for the target block. Additionally, The snapshot-streaming implementation requires `RunFileReader` to have no whole-run member, keeps `cur_block.size() <= kRunHardCapBlockSize`, and bounds every ranged request by `kRunHardCapBlockSize + 64 * 1024` plus the footer allowance.

topic: fully idle GC round with no journal changes and no retired entries performs zero
canonical_claim: A fully idle GC round with no journal changes and no retired entries performs zero run-object GETs and PUTs.

topic: GC rebuild reconstructs cursors and edges but reclaims nothing
canonical_claim: A GC rebuild reconstructs cursors and edges but reclaims nothing; blobs not named by a surviving manifest are retained as `unaccounted`.; `Gc::rebuildBaseline` writes only the GC plane—runs, seals, and `gc/state`—and never modifies ref shards, manifests, or blobs or deletes content. Additionally, `SYSTEM CAS GC REBUILD` writes only the GC plane, namely `gc/state` and `gc/gen/*` artifacts, and does not touch ref shards, manifests, or blobs or delete anything during the rebuild itself.

topic: CAS has exactly one blob-body deletion site
canonical_claim: CAS has exactly one blob-body deletion site: the pre-CAS `pending_deletes` phase of a GC round, limited to entries marked `delete_pending` by a previously published round.; The `pending_deletes` phase is the single content-delete site for exact-token deletes of previously published `delete_pending` entries.
